solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Chopper posted reportedly to find grave in France? (6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so the words are to be taken by their sound

annotation.surface: Someone seeks a grave in France and is told an axe has been sent by post.
annotation.walkthrough: Said together, 'axe-sent' is ACCENT. 'Grave' is not a burial place but the grave accent of French spelling, as in è; the question mark flags the example.
annotation.definitionFit: The grave is one of the accents written over French letters.

entries.clue: Elevation of opinion, Liberal for the first time (8)

indicatorNotes.for the first time: L goes in place of the first T, the first 'time' in ATTITUDE

blocks.note: an attitude is an opinion or outlook
T is time, so the L goes where the first T stood

annotation.surface: A Liberal voice lifts the tone of a debate for once.
annotation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time, so 'for the first time' means in place of the first T, not 'never before'.
annotation.definitionFit: Altitude is height or elevation above sea level.

entries.clue: Rant about cutting price difference (8)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters of RANT are turned about into a new order
indicatorNotes.cutting: the rearranged letters cut into COST, splitting it

annotation.surface: Someone rails against a price cut that makes a difference.
annotation.walkthrough: CO + NTRA + ST. 'Rant about' reads as a complaint, but 'about' is telling you to rearrange RANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A contrast is a noticeable difference between things.

entries.clue: Digital protection not available in libraries initially (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of 'in libraries'

annotation.surface: Some digital security software cannot be had in libraries at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers; here it means of the fingers (digits), which a nail protects.
annotation.definitionFit: A fingernail shields the tip of a finger, or digit.

entries.clue: Rider‘s heartless obsession (8)

indicatorNotes.heartless: the heart, or middle letter, is taken out

blocks.note: the middle letter C of ADDICTION goes

annotation.surface: A cold-hearted horse rider is fixated on something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rider' looks like someone on a horse; it is the other sense, a clause added to a document or bill.
annotation.definitionFit: A rider is an addition attached to a contract or bill.

entries.clue: Bubbly tonic appearing in journals and word books (12)

indicatorNotes.Bubbly: fizzing letters are stirred up, so TONIC is rearranged
indicatorNotes.appearing in: the rearranged letters sit inside DIARIES

annotation.surface: Fizzy tonic water turns up in magazines and word books.
annotation.walkthrough: DI + CTION + ARIES. 'Bubbly tonic' reads as a drink, but 'bubbly' is the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: reference books that list and explain words.

entries.clue: Crown removed from pitch pine (4)

indicatorNotes.Crown removed from: the crown is the top, so the first letter of a down answer goes

annotation.surface: The top of a pitch pine tree has been lopped off.
annotation.walkthrough: Pitch pine is a real tree, so 'pine' seems to be a noun; it is the verb, to long for.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to be itching to do something is to yearn for it.

entries.clue: Principles of current agreements (6)

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A question about the principles behind the deals now on the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as present-day agreements; it is the physics symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: Ideals are the principles someone aims to live by.

entries.clue: Finally Gordon Brown becomes less sensitive (6)

annotation.definitionNote: NUMBER here is the comparative of numb, said 'NUMMER'

indicatorNotes.Finally: take the last letter of Gordon

blocks.note: umber is an earthy brown colour

annotation.surface: In the end, former Prime Minister Gordon Brown grows thick-skinned.
annotation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was a British Prime Minister, so the name reads as one unit; it splits. NUMBER is not the counting word but 'more numb'.
annotation.definitionFit: Number, meaning more numb, is less sensitive.

entries.clue: Sinner right to withdraw, taking time for return game (6)

indicatorNotes.to withdraw: to withdraw is to pull out, as a player pulls out of a match, so right (R) pulls out of SINNER
indicatorNotes.taking: the remaining letters take on T
indicatorNotes.for return: the whole is then read backwards

annotation.surface: Jannik Sinner pulls out, buying time before a rematch.
annotation.walkthrough: SINNE + T = SINNET, reversed. Jannik Sinner is a leading tennis player, so the answer is part of the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the racket sport scored in games, sets and matches, and the one Sinner plays.

entries.clue: Trump’s enforcers’ best course? (3,5)

blocks.note: ICE is US Immigration and Customs Enforcement
the cream is the best of anything

annotation.surface: Asks what the best route is for President Trump's immigration agents.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' seems to mean a path to take; it is a course of a meal, and the question mark marks ice cream as one example of a dessert course.
annotation.definitionFit: Ice cream may be served as the dessert course of a meal.

entries.clue: Proved villain’s handled without prejudice, ultimately (12)

indicatorNotes.without: the letter is left out of TREATED
indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of prejudice

blocks.note: a demon is a villain, plus 's
TREATED loses the E that ends prejudicE

annotation.surface: A villain was dealt with fairly, with no prejudice in the end, and the case was proved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without prejudice' is a legal phrase, but here only its last letter E matters: TREATED drops it.
annotation.definitionFit: To demonstrate something is to prove it.

entries.clue: Food that could be sweet and sour (4)

blocks.note: a pastry case with a filling, often of fruit or jam

annotation.surface: A dish that could taste either sweet or sour.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like sweet-and-sour cooking, but 'sweet and sour' is split: the first half defines the pastry, the second the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry that is often sweet; tart also means sour.

entries.clue: Do a runner, unlike criminals? (5)

blocks.note: British slang for running off, often without paying; a two-word slang phrase
criminals are crooked, so their opposite is above board: a short informal word for lawful

annotation.surface: Running away, which is exactly what criminals do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do a runner' and 'leg it' are British slang for running away, often without paying. Split as LEG IT it is the escape; read whole, LEGIT means lawful.
annotation.definitionFit: Legit is short for legitimate, the opposite of criminal; to leg it is to run away.

entries.clue: Caught rather indecent bishop leaving this? (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the bishop's letter B leaves BLUE

annotation.surface: A bishop is caught out leaving something rather racy.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is 'this', the clue itself: the question mark points at the thing you are reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Self-reference: 'this' points at the very sentence the solver is reading, and that thing is the crossword's own hint.

entries.clue: Farah’s back going after record for racing here (5)

indicatorNotes.going after: the reversed piece comes after EP

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Mo Farah, the British distance runner: MO'S

annotation.surface: Runner Mo Farah is back, chasing a record at a racecourse.
annotation.walkthrough: Epsom is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby. 'Farah's back' reads as his return; it is his first name, Mo's, reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a racecourse, so racing happens here.

entries.clue: Faced brewing espresso without the kick? (5)

indicatorNotes.brewing: letters that brew are stirred together into something new

annotation.surface: Someone is confronted with a cup of espresso that has no caffeine.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as one example: decaf can be any coffee, not only espresso.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the kick of coffee is caffeine, and coffee with it removed has none.

entries.clue: Upset to be sacked? (12)

blocks.note: let down, saddened by a hope not met
the reverse of appointed: removed from a post

annotation.surface: Being fired leaves anyone unhappy.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented: read as DIS-APPOINTED, the opposite of being appointed, which the question mark admits.
annotation.definitionFit: Disappointed means let down or upset.

entries.clue: Hikes aircraft prices? (8)

blocks.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

annotation.surface: Asks whether airlines are raising fares.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hikes' looks like price rises beside 'prices'; it is the verb, to travel a long way, as birds do.
annotation.definitionFit: A creature that migrates hikes a long way to a new place.

entries.clue: Police blocking border is obligatory (8)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the police sit in the border like a roadblock, inside END

blocks.note: an end is a border or edge

annotation.surface: Police stationed at a frontier checkpoint are compulsory.
annotation.walkthrough: EN(FORCE)D. 'Border' first suggests a frontier; here it is simply an end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a rule that is compelled by authority leaves no choice, so it is compulsory.

entries.clue: Primarily critical renovations ordered for maintenance (12)

indicatorNotes.Primarily: take the first letter of critical
indicatorNotes.ordered: the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Urgent repairs have been commissioned to keep a building in good order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as commissioned; it is the signal to rearrange RENOVATIONS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the upkeep and protection of buildings or nature.

entries.clue: Church plea to refurbish place of worship (6)

annotation.surface: A church appeals for funds to restore its building.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a church restoration appeal, and the answer fits the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small church, or a room set aside for prayer.

entries.clue: Provide education for current class (6)

blocks.note: a form is a school class

annotation.surface: Teaching for the present year group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' usually gives I in crosswords; here it is IN, as in fashionable. A form is a school class or year in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pass on knowledge or facts to someone.

entries.clue: Give worker cards (4)

blocks.note: to pass something over to someone
a manual labourer, as on a farm or a ship
the set of cards dealt to one player

annotation.surface: An instruction to deal a worker some cards.
annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions in three words: to give, a worker, and a set of cards.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: the verb to pass over, a manual labourer, and the cards dealt to a player.

entries.clue: Not against production of Oliver in Oxford college (5)

indicatorNotes.Not: 'not against' means without the word for against, so V (versus) is dropped from OLIVER
indicatorNotes.production of: the letters are made into something new

annotation.surface: A college in Oxford puts on a show of Oliver! that is not controversial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Production of Oliver' looks like a staging of the musical; it rearranges the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a college founded in 1326 on Oxford's High Street, one of the university's oldest.

entries.clue: Clear notice protects Florentine banker (4)

indicatorNotes.protects: the outer words enclose, and so protect, the answer

annotation.surface: A plain warning guards a Renaissance banker from Florence.
annotation.walkthrough: A banker is something with banks: the Arno is the river flowing through Florence, not a Medici moneylender.
annotation.definitionFit: The Arno is Florence's river, and a river has banks.

entries.clue: Sport in bankruptcy (4)

annotation.surface: A sports club has gone bust.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is part of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: losing everything you own is financial collapse.

entries.clue: Time Out article (4)

indicatorNotes.Out: letters put out of place are rearranged

annotation.surface: A piece in Time Out, the London listings magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: Time Out is a London listings magazine, so the clue reads as one article in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single piece in a newspaper, or a single thing on a list.

entries.clue: Ace channels for commodities (8)

blocks.note: an ace is an expert, a pro

annotation.surface: A top trader's routes for getting goods to market.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Channels for commodities' reads as supply chains, but 'for' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: goods made or grown to be sold.

entries.clue: Small attic needs converting still (6)

indicatorNotes.needs converting: converting changes ATTIC into a new arrangement

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A little loft still has to be turned into a room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' sits at the end looking like 'yet'; it is the definition, meaning motionless.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: motionless, unchanging.

entries.clue: French newspaper includes article that is refreshing (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the drink by what it does: something that is refreshing

indicatorNotes.includes: LE MONDE takes the A inside it

annotation.surface: A French newspaper runs a piece that is a breath of fresh air.
annotation.walkthrough: LE MON(A)DE. 'Article' reads as a newspaper story, but it is the grammar word A.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a cold, fizzy or still citrus drink, the kind reached for on a hot day.

entries.clue: Delighted to see goddess featuring in poster (6)

indicatorNotes.featuring in: the goddess appears inside the poster, AD

blocks.note: the Muses were goddesses of the arts

annotation.surface: Pleased to spot a goddess pictured on a billboard.
annotation.walkthrough: A(MUSE)D. The Muse, a goddess, fits inside the advert.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pleased and entertained by something.
